summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with nausea, vomiting, black stools, and fevers. She has chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML) on Gleevec. Workup revealed progression to blast crisis, confirmed by bone marrow biopsy showing 16% blasts. Initial treatment with HyperCVAD and dasatinib was switched to 7+3 induction after immunophenotyping confirmed myeloblastic crisis. The hospital course was complicated by neutropenic fever, and blood cultures grew Leptotrichia trevosani, leading to broad-spectrum antibiotics and replacement of her Hickman line with a PICC. She developed severe nausea and vomiting, resulting in a Mallory-Weiss tear confirmed by endoscopy. Her nausea was controlled with PPI, Zofran, and Zyprexa. She also had pneumonia and sinusitis, both managed supportively. Repeat bone marrow biopsies showed decreasing blasts, with no clear population detected by day 49. She improved clinically, became afebrile, and her counts recovered. She was discharged home on oral metronidazole for 9 days, with plans to restart dasatinib and proceed to transplant evaluation.
problems: Acute myeloid leukemia, without mention of having achieved remission
Pneumonia due to other gram-negative bacteria
Fever presenting with conditions classified elsewhere
Other and unspecified infection due to central venous catheter
